body:
* **UniProt Keyword ID and label:**
Oxidoreductase (KW-0560)

The following Dmel protein (TrEMBL) entries have the keyword 'Oxidoreductase' applied and therefore get the GO annotation 'oxidoreductase activity'.
In all cases, the keyword is imported from an EMBL sequence entry.
But, in all cases, I can't see any (good) evidence for oxidoreductase activity in those EMBL entries.

@Antonialock can you or David C see why the KW is applied in these cases?

-- | -- | -- | -- | --
FBgn0010516 | wal | Q7KN94 | AF58627.1 | Don't see any evidence
FBgn0033820 | CG4716 | A1Z9B4/Q7JRN6 | AAM68605.1/AAF58393.1 | Don't see any evidence for this.
FBgn0037298 | CG2604 | Q9VN86 | AAF52062.1 | Note line contains 'dehydrogenase'?
FBgn0038038 | CG5167 | Q9VG81 | AAF54804.1 | Note line contains 'dehydrogenase'?
FBgn0034105 | CG7755 | A1ZAD2 | AAF58023.2 | Don't see any evidence
FBgn0035046 | ND-19 | Q9W125 | AAF47252.1 | Product line contains 'oxidoreductase' and note line contains 'dehydrogenase'?
FBgn0034645 | ND-B12 | Q9W2E8 | AAF46744.1 | Product line contains 'oxidoreductase' and note line contains 'dehydrogenase'?
FBgn0033570 | ND-B14 | Q7JZK1 | AAF58729.1 | Product line contains 'oxidoreductase' and note line contains 'dehydrogenase'?
FBgn0033961 | ND-B15 | Q6IDF5 | AAF58210.1 |  Product line contains 'oxidoreductase' and note line contains 'dehydrogenase'?


As noted, some EMBL records contain the string 'oxidoreductase' or 'dehydrogenase' in the product line or note line, but I hope these are not being used to apply the 'oxidoreductase' KW - many gene products may contain a string like that because they are a complex subunit, or an assembly factor, or a pseudo enzyme, but not be catalytically active themselves.

Thanks!

author: sjm41
body:
Adding a few notes from the related email thread between me and @Antonialock (following her own chats with Jie Luo), for the record:

- EC/KW assignments from EMBL sequence records for TrEMBL entries are NOT re-run automatically. There are too many TrEMBL entries for this to be done each UP release.
- This means that if an EC number in an EMBL record is changed/added/removed, this isn't automatically reflected in the the associated TrEMBL record at UniProt or any GO annotations inferred from it (EC2GO, KW2GO)
- However, if individual TrEMBL records are known to be problematic/updated, then they can be "re-TrEMBLed" on a case-by-case basis. Need to give UP devs a list.
- It is also possible to "re-TrEMBL" an entire specified proteome (this is what we've asked for the Dmel case, since many EMBL records have been updated with their associated EC numbers in the last few years, and not reflected in TrEMBL, and therefore UniProt GO annotation pipelines)
